name: Milagu Kuzhambu
subtitle: a dark, peppery tamarind gravy roasted from whole spices, the household cure-all

ingredients.qty: a lime-sized ball, soaked in 300ml hot water

ingredients.note: the whole point of the dish; do not reduce it
for the roast, not for body
stirred into the roasted spices at the end
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free
the quantity is deliberate; this gravy is preserved by its oil

prepNotes: Soak the tamarind in hot water for 20 minutes, then squeeze it out and strain. Discard the fibres and seeds.
Roast the spices on a genuinely low flame. This is the step the whole dish rests on and it cannot be hurried.
Milagu kuzhambu tastes better the day after it is made. Consider cooking it a day ahead.

steps.text: Dry roast the peppercorns, the three dals, the red chillies and fenugreek seeds in a kadhai over low heat for 6 to 8 minutes until the dals are reddish gold and the pepper smells sharp.
steps.tip: If the fenugreek darkens past honey brown the whole pot turns bitter. It is the first thing to burn.

steps.text: Turn off the heat, stir in the coriander powder and one sprig of curry leaves, and let the residual heat toast them for 30 seconds.
Cool completely, then grind to a fine powder in a dry blender.
steps.tip: Grind only when cold. Warm spices smear into a paste in the jar.

steps.text: Heat the sesame oil in the same kadhai and crackle the mustard seeds, then add the remaining curry leaves and the asafoetida.
Pour in the strained tamarind water with the turmeric and salt and bring to a rolling boil.
Boil hard, uncovered, for 8 minutes to cook out the raw edge of the tamarind.
Whisk the ground spice powder with 60ml water to a slurry and stir it in.
steps.tip: Making a slurry first stops the powder from seizing into lumps in the hot liquid.

steps.text: Simmer 10 to 12 minutes over low heat until the gravy thickens and the oil separates and floats in a dark ring on top.
steps.tip: The floating oil is the finish line. Take it off any earlier and it will not keep.

steps.text: Stir in the jaggery, cook 2 minutes more and take off the heat.
Serve a spoonful over hot rice with a poriyal and a papad.

storage: Because of the oil and tamarind this keeps 10 days refrigerated in a glass jar, and improves for the first three. Always spoon it out with a dry spoon. Reheat only the portion you need.
